title: Finances — choose the composition
question: A monthly budget: paychecks logged as they land, categories with limits, a transaction log, and three charts (cash left through the month, income vs expenses by month, spent vs limit). Same world. Lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: One ruled table, categories that open
options.lineage: the household account book: one page per month, a row per heading
options.thesis: The month is a single wide ruled table — one row per category with limit, spent, left and an ink bar; a row opens to reveal its transactions and an inline add line. Income sits as a short block above it (expected, landed so far, next expected). Charts run beneath.
materials: ruled table rows with ink bars
one white card for the cash-left chart
options.viewport: Band: 'Finances', italic 'September · $2,140 left of $3,200 · 16 days'. Paper: 'Income' as two ruled rows (expected $4,200 · landed $2,900 · next paycheck Fri 25) with 'Log a paycheck'; then 'Categories' table: Rent, Groceries, Transport, Fun, Savings… each with limit / spent / left / bar; Groceries open showing its transactions and an add line. Below: cash-left card (line to month end, rent marked), then income vs expenses (6 months) beside spent vs limit bars.
options.risk: Transactions are hidden until a row opens, so 'what did I buy yesterday' takes a click; the table needs care at 390px.

regions.label: Income: expected · landed · next  + Log a paycheck
Categories table: limit · spent · left · bar (Groceries open → its transactions + add line)

options.label: Three numbers, then two columns
options.lineage: the month's balance sheet: headline figures over the detail
options.thesis: A headline row of three serif figures — Income so far, Spent, Left — sets the month; beneath, two columns: categories with limit bars on the left, the transaction log with an always-visible add line on the right. Charts sit at the bottom.
materials: a ruled transaction ledger with inline add
one white card for the cash-left chart
options.viewport: Band: 'Finances', italic date. Paper: three figures across the top (Income so far $2,900 of $4,200 expected · Spent $1,060 · Left $2,140), each with a one-line note; left 6/12 'Categories' ruled rows with bars and limits (editable); right 6/12 'This month' log — add line (what, amount, category, date) then transactions newest first; paychecks logged in the same ledger as income lines. Below: cash-left card, income vs expenses, spent vs limit.
options.risk: Reads as a report at first glance; the add line must be obviously an input or the page feels read-only.

regions.label: This month: add line + transactions (income and expenses)

options.label: Income page, expenses page
options.lineage: a double-entry book lying open: money in on the left, money out on the right
options.thesis: Two pages with a gutter. Left page is Income: expected for the month, each paycheck or gig logged as it lands, a running total and 'next expected'. Right page is Expenses: categories with limits and bars, and the transaction log beneath with its add line. Charts run across both pages at the bottom.
materials: two paper pages with a centre gutter
one white card for the cash-left chart
options.viewport: Band: 'Finances', italic 'September · $2,140 left'. Left page (5/12): 'Money in' — expected $4,200; paychecks: Fri 4 $1,450 · Fri 11 $1,450 · Sat 12 gig $120; 'Log a paycheck' line; landed $2,900, next expected Fri 25. Right page (7/12): 'Money out' — categories with limit bars, then the log with add line. Bottom, full width: cash-left card; income vs expenses; spent vs limit.
options.risk: Income rarely has more than a few lines, so the left page can look empty mid-month; the gutter is decoration unless it carries the running balance.

regions.label: Money in: expected · paychecks logged · next expected · Log a paycheck
Money out: categories with limit bars
Money out: transaction log + add line
